reviewMethod: Inspected all 48 frames through four 12-frame contact sheets, then inspected the three full-resolution key stills and full-resolution frames 22, 24, 26, 28, 30 and 32 around the derived detachment event.

questions.observation: The unchanged wide cause shot clearly establishes the worn basketball, three distinct filled bottles, attached caps, court and scale cues.
The new fixed contact camera preserves continuous closure into collision without a visible gap or transform jump.
The blue target bottle retains its silver cap through the pre-contact frames.
After contact, the silver-black cap visibly separates from the blue bottle neck beginning at the derived frame 24.
Frames 22-32 show one continuous solver-owned cap trajectory down and away from the neck without teleporting.
The detached object remains a recognizable small cylindrical metal cap, distinct from the larger ball and bottles.
All three bottles respond continuously; two fall in different directions and one remains upright in an asymmetric, unstaged final arrangement.
The cap roll is subtle but clearly adds a secondary causal beat without explosive motion or decorative debris.
The effect shot contains all three response bottles and places the detached cap beside the open blue neck with useful screen separation.
Warm court light, cool fill, reflections and stable derived camera progression remain filmic without particles, shake or fake post effects.

comparisonToAttempt11: The physics is byte-projection-identical; only the derived camera changed. The previously hidden cap is now readable throughout its separation and roll.
